caption: Trees before: the twelve species that each had their own hand-written generator.
Trees after: the same species regrown on the blob generator, crowns built from lit blobs of leaf stamps.
Broadleaf tree crowns before the bold pixel-art style pass.
The same crowns under the bold style: fewer, chunkier leaf clusters in three hue-shifted tones.
Broadleaf trees before the leaf-clump pass: crowns built the old way.
After: crowns made of lit leaf clumps, and life below them too, ivy, moss and low boughs on every trunk.
A party campfire before the party reaches it: cold and dark, waiting by the path.
The moment the wave arrives: the campfire whooshes alight in a burst of warm light and sparks.
Settled in: the fire burns steadily, lighting the ground and the party pieces around it.
The dodge before her magic got its night palette: she just jumps.
After: the dodge leaves a glowing afterimage and her broom throws sparks.
Dream bubbles restyled as soft, round, amber thought bubbles holding the wished-for creature's sigil.
The boar's evolution with its surface texture: fur gathered into small tufted cells so the light breaks along them, coarse on the piglet and fine on the legend.
The snail's evolution, from a near-clear shell to a towering legend the forest has built on its back.
The ram's evolution, from a curly lamb to the thicket-grown legend with bronze thorned horns and brambles over its back.
The wolf's evolution, from a round pup to the spirit-fire legend with a spiky, flaming mane.
The woodlouse's evolution, from a pale baby to a leaf-litter fortress crowned with moonstone spires.
The heron builder's wading bird at every level, on slender stilt legs.
The heron and its sleeping legend, the second area and creature made purely from data.
Throwing 💌s before the magic pass: they simply appear and vanish.
After: each 💌 trails sparkles, puffs where it lands and blooms rose on a hit.
The live rig: a wolf put together each frame from baked torso, head and leg pieces, its legs stepping as two-bone chains through walk, turn, charge and leap.
Party animals got little party shoes; here a boar in boots walks, turns, charges and leaps on the live rig, its shoes stepping with each leg.
The moor from the treetops before the art director's second round: the canopy sinks into the dark.
After: moonlight catches the tops of the trees, so flying high finally looks like flying over a moonlit forest.
A broken old road running through a birch wood: one of the ten path kinds that wind between the areas.
From the treetops an old railway line cuts through the forest, lamplight along its edge.
The first props grown from genomes: standing stones, cairns, pools and broken trunks, hand-made versions beside their generated variants, with the witch for scale.
Fallen logs, mushroom rings and stone circles, each grown from a seed by the prop generator.
Boulders and mounds joined the prop generator: each comes in several seeded shapes, half sunk, cracked and mossed, instead of one hand-drawn sprite repeated.
The monoline animal sigils: every species' sigil is the animal itself drawn as one clean line, in its area's neon.
Legendary sigils: twice as wide, more of the animal, with a crowned gold border, for the legends of each area.
Creature sizes before the size curves: babies, young, adults and legends grew in uneven steps.
After the size curves: each species now grows from baby to legend in clear, even steps.
Rigged stag legs before: strings of balls.
After: smooth limbs with proper hocks on the hind legs.
Walking under the fern forest: before, the crowns round her vanished in hard rings; after, they fade softly tree by tree.
The soft reveal in motion: crowns melt away one by one as she walks through the forest on foot.
Spooky lighting 1: a cold dark wood with the party as the only warm light.
Before the spooky lighting pass: a late-game party scene lit evenly, every corner of the wood as bright as the dancefloor.
Spooky lighting 3: each area type gets its own fog, tint and mist.
Spooky lighting, step one: the wood goes cold and dark, so the party becomes the warm light you fly towards.
Step two: the party throws warm pools of light round its soundsystems and lights, islands of colour in the night.
Step four: a thin moonlight rim on every character, so the witch and the animals still read against the dark.
The treehouse before the tilt-shift: every part of the picture in the same sharp focus.
With the tilt-shift on, the top and bottom of the screen blur away, so the forest reads like a model village seen up close.
The witch generator: a witch as genome data. Ours is drawn exactly, and every other is a new witch within the limits, hats, brooms, cloaks and all.
Witch hats: no hat and eleven more, from a cowboy hat and a crown to boppers and a traffic cone, flying and standing.
Generated party witches: bigger brims, longer cloaks and a wide spread of looks for the witches who fly in to dance.
Lasers fan out from the dancefloor ring into the night, an early sign the forest was going to be a rave.
Party witches flying in over the dancefloor as its tiles blaze pink, one for every soundsystem that is up and playing.
Rising past the treehouse's storeys: a round timber tower with glowing windows and a ring of fairy lights.
The early dancefloor from behind a soundsystem: a round floor of glowing blue tiles and a laser beam sweeping across it.
A campfire in a birch wood, its light falling across the pale trunks in dithered pixel steps.
Her own light: a warm pool round the witch on the forest floor, so she is never lost in the dark.
Thirty areas side by side from the treetops: every kind of forest, moor and clearing in the game, each with its own trees, floor and colours.
An overgrown football pitch, goals and all: part of the old modern world the forest has swallowed.
The witch lit by the world around her, before and after: campfire, neon and moonlight now colour her sprite.
The bend, off, subtle and strong: the world curving away toward the top of the screen so the night sky shows over the forest.
Castle ruins in the woods, with wild creatures wandering round: one of the large scenes built from landmark pieces.
Attack feel, frame by frame: a wind-up crouch, a lunge, a squash and tumble, and a little star where the hit lands.
The badger growing up, from a cub that is all face to a legend carrying standing stones on its back: the moor's walking stones.
A trail of footprints wandering across the sand and fading out, among shells and starfish.
Where the woods meet the beach: palms, beach grass and scalloped bushes instead of a hard wall of trees.
The sea before and after: too dark at first, then a calm moonlit blue-teal that mirrors the sky.
The boar, pilot of the evolution kit: from a striped piglet to a legend with curling tusks and wisps of flame.
Fourteen new brooms for the creator, from a missile and a jet bike to a canoe, a bicycle and a gyrocopter.
Seeing her under the trees, before and after: a round window cut in the canopy, then a ragged hole opened crown by crown.
Her light on the treetops: a warm amber pool following her across the crowns, no longer lime green.
A wardrobe of starting looks for the witch, each a different hat, cloak, broom and palette, made to go together.
Creature expressions up close: every species can look neutral, angry, happy or dazed, drawn right into its face.
The fen and its newt: the first area type and creature built entirely from data, with no new drawing code.
Fantasy flora from the treetops: glowcap mushroom trees lighting up a patch of night forest.
Ten new tree species grown by the genome generator, blob crowns filled with leaf stamps, three of them fantasy.
Pixel wind: each blob of a crown sways as a whole, a whole pixel at a time, out of step with its neighbours.
The fox's evolution from a fluffy kit to the shrine's many-tailed kitsune legend, each stage its own design, not just bigger.
Creature genomes let one species wear many curated coats (frost, ember, shadow, gold, moss, rose, ash) with no redrawing.
Ground variants: each area's floor grown from a ground genome, in several variants so it no longer visibly repeats.
Party ground at home: picnic blankets, tables with chairs and tall balloons scattered round the dancefloor.
Sleeping legends, batch 3: lynx, otter, beaver, ram, squirrel, dormouse and salamander, sunk and mossed so they pass for boulders and logs.
Legends' back trees: little generated forests growing on the sleeping legends' backs, by species and seed.
A sleeping legend's sleepy face, mostly 😴, mid-yawn in its circle.
Home from the treetops under the spooky lighting: the treehouse glowing amid party lights and ley lines.
Round three of the lighting reviews: a paler moon fill without the dotted pattern, and the witch properly lit in the bold pixel style.
Up close on a squirrel, before and after: the moonlight rim picks out its silhouette from the forest floor.
The tilt-shift blur, before and after: the miniature-world blur now lets the stars show through softly at the top of the screen.
The character creator's longer cloaks and scarves: past the old limits they stream and ripple behind her in flight.
A sigil glowing as she sets it down on the ground, part of giving all her magic one night-time palette.
One moon for the whole game: a time-lapse of it rising behind the far forest and crossing the sky over a run.
The newt, from baby to legend: the first creature (with its fen) made entirely from data, no new drawing code.
The 💌s, hearts and chat bubbles now blur with the tilt-shift too, so they sit in the miniature world instead of floating over it.
Owl evolution: from a downy owlet to the legend's moonlit cloak, each level its own design rather than just bigger.
Party animals dancing on the beat once they've joined.
Guests spread out round the dancefloor instead of piling up in one heap.
Picnic blankets, picnic tables with chairs and tall balloons on long strings, scattered over partified ground.
The party relics: six giant glowing bottles, half-buried in the forest floor, each with its own sigil to wake a legend happy.
Little party shoes on party animals: trainers, glitter, platforms, heels, boots and light-ups, on hooves, paws and claws.
Party witches fly in to the dancefloor and roam round it, dancing, drinking and resting.
The party from above: witches swoop round the dancefloor below the treehouse.
Their swoops leave bright rainbow trails of glow behind them.
Spinning 💌s before (rotated smoothly) and after (redrawn in whole art pixels), a small change that keeps the pixel look honest.
The ley line redrawn in art pixels with smooth light, and brighter, so it reads as part of the pixel world.
A soundsystem set beside a stump throne in its clearing, from an early pass on where set pieces stand.
Ponds that read as water, not holes: a moonlit rim, a sheen of sky, a muddy lip and glints.
Footbridges, rope bridges and root bridges each got three generated variants, so no two stream crossings look quite alike.
The party's bunting, balloon bunches and paper lanterns, now varied by the prop generator so every partified clearing is dressed a little differently.
Set pieces from genomes: sunken punts, rickety jetties, rings of stones or stumps and mossy heaps, each sized to sit in a clearing.
The silhouette check: every adult creature beside its shadow shape, so no two species can be mistaken for each other at game size.
Smoke from every fire: soft moonlit puffs rise well above the treetops, drifting with the wind and thinning away.
The canopy cut-out round the witch: a hard ring of whole trees before, a soft, wide, wandering fade after.
A gentler tilt-shift: half the blur and a wider sharp band, so more of the dancefloor stays in focus.
The moon through the tilt-shift at every phase, from a thin crescent to full, still readable through the blur.
Her flight trail over the treetops: a fading glow in the colour of the area she flies over.
Ground-cover tufts for six areas in today's style and the two pixel-art styles, bold and ref: fewer, bolder stamps.
The bot game: sit back and watch the skilled bot play a whole run, flying, talking and fighting on its own.
A young boar's speed over a charge, before and after: charges got weight, winding up and carrying through instead of snapping on and off.
Signature moves for 19 more species, traced from above: backing off, pounces, flanking and darting.
Combat round 13: a boar's charge now carries further across the dancefloor, a real threat to dodge.
After the Party's Over: the wood's night sounds.
...and the sleepers' snores.
The Boot, sped up: the home speakers turn on one by one and each brings in one of the intro's twelve layers on the next bar line.
All twelve runestones crackling into life as speakers, one after another.
Walking into the wolf legend's circle: the music muffles and slows like a tape winding down, while the legend's own layer plays on at full speed.
The owl's circle: every legend has its own patterns, melody and octave in the music's key.
The moth's circle.
The deep forest scene before the mix pass: the music far off, a sleeping legend's moans, a wind-up, a charge.
The same scene after the mix pass, every sound set to its target loudness over the music.
Thirty seconds of a scripted run: the boot at home.
Wave three: the arc has moved on through its sections.
A siege: the siege parts come in by how near the fight at the soundsystem is.
The party spell's scroll bursting.
A pond at night.
The sea, heard as she nears the beach.
Every species' call in turn: speech without words, a voice through vowel formants, each family with its own call style.
The witch's babble: each 💌 is a syllable, each burst a phrase lifting at the end.
A sleeping elk legend's lament: whale song, long gliding moans in a big reverb.
The flourish when a legend is invited (each level has its own).
The creator's bedroom, twice the size, with her look editor beside it: the place every run now begins.
Walking about the bedroom with WASD, her pool of light following her across the floorboards.
The bedroom character creator before its layout pass: the room and the menu at different pixel scales.
After: one pixel scale for room and menu, the Coven Rush title on top and the 🎶 party spell scroll waiting in the corner.
The opening: the witch on the dark dancefloor with one button, CAST THE PARTY SPELL.
The party spell cast: the pulse runs round the runestones clockwise, turning each one on as it passes.
Booted: the home ring lit and the ley lines glowing off into the forest.
The first character creator, in the witch's early treehouse room: dress her up while the forest loads behind the scenes.
Character creator 2 moved into a cosy isometric bedroom, with wider sliders, rainbow colours, more hats and bags.
The creator's broom box in its finished form: missiles, hobby horses, jet bikes, canoes and gyrocopters alongside the classic broomstick.
How a run begins: behind her decks in the treehouse, one button, CAST THE PARTY SPELL.
Casting the party spell: she raises her hands, sparkles burst, and the night begins.
The party spell as a scroll with a glowing note on it, waiting in the corner of her bedroom; nearing it, the paper trembles and the screen darkens.
Casting the party spell: the scroll grows to fill the screen, crackles, bursts, and the night begins.
An early start screen: a title, a What's new list and a Coming up column, all text.
The start screen as it became: Coven Rush, opening straight into her bedroom, with the character creator on the left and the spell scroll waiting bottom right.
Where a run starts: the witch behind her decks in the treehouse's cutaway DJ booth.
The second treehouse: she sits behind her decks in a round booth, neon strips glowing along the desk.
Treehouse v2 from the treetops: a timber tower of lit storeys climbing a giant tree.
The very first start screen: a plain text panel over the forest saying "fly the witch round the forest at night", with the controls and a What's new list. Everything later grew out of this.
Early version of the start: she stands behind the decks in the treehouse's cutaway DJ booth, the party gear around her.
The treehouse from below, with the glowing pentagram of the runestone ring on the ground in front of it.
A cosy start: the witch sits on the porch of her caravan-like treehouse, fairy lights strung beside her.
Her messy treehouse bedroom, drawn isometric, with PARTY TONIGHT bunting over the bed: the place you dress your witch.
While the game loads, the witch potters about her room: her idle moments made the loading screen feel alive.
The first character creator: dress your witch in her treehouse under PARTY TONIGHT bunting, a mirror at the side.
Creator done, game on: she appears behind her decks in the treehouse's DJ booth, ready to start the party.
The character creator reorganised into a box per item, one open at a time, each with its own colour picker.
The creator beside the witch's cosy bedroom: you dress her up before the night begins.
In the bedroom she walks over to whatever you're changing: the wardrobe, the hat stand, the broom.
When the first wave comes, the full moon on the dancefloor flares out into the party's switch-on.
Before the first wave, the dancefloor shows only the moon's phase in muted tiles, new moon to full.
Mid-cast in the DJ booth, amber and rose sparkles bursting round her.
An early look at the treehouse settled beside the dancefloor's glowing ring.
The boot pulse runs round the dancefloor, turning each small runestone into a speaker as the home ring powers up.
The hero dancefloor booting up: its glass tiles flickering into life before the party.
Party level 1: a calm pattern of a few lit tiles.
Party level 4, a full rave: the floor spins with purple and yellow spokes.
The HUD before: a wave timer bar and a cue toward the dancefloor.
After: a game clock at the top and a single 🎶 wave pointer toward the ley line's pulse.
An angry legend's long charge, 1: thundering in toward the witch.
2: missing and braking past her.
3: walking back home to its area.

The whole route on six seeds: the older varied order (left) beside the spiral (right), blue for the first waves to pink for the last, crossings ringed red. Under each pair, distance from home by wave.
The ley line leaving home on six seeds: clockwise round the ring of speakers, off to the right and on to the first runestone, never over the dancefloor.
A wave arriving, first frame: the area's little runestone glade is still quiet as the party's magic begins to circle.
A few moments later the ring of pink sparkles has spread round the area: the party has taken it over.
Where the six party relics land on one map: one just inside home's edge, the rest scattered at least 150 m apart.
The game on a phone from the start: the treehouse squeezed into a tall screen, with on-screen buttons for flying, rising and sigils under her thumbs.
Flying with a full leash: the sigils of every creature that joined her stack above her head as she crosses the woods.
A fight in the dark: wild creatures rushing the witch while her party animals hold the line in blue rings.
Runestone beacons, before and after: the rings of symbols gone, each column of light now appearing only when the ley line reaches it.
The dodge as a blink: she vanishes in a faint ring of motes and reappears ten metres on.
The aim reticle up close: a ring for her 💌 range, with a blue arc filling as the dodge recharges.
The dodge now flies toward the mouse cursor, with a little diamond on the ground showing where she'll land.
A happy creature carries its sigil rune at its feet; the witch picks the rune up and the creature joins her leash for good.
Knocked out, the witch drops her hat where she fell, so she can fly back, find it and pop it back on.
Every 💌 that lands counts: a ring of envelopes orbits the creature being invited, filling up as she charms it.
Slow motion: 💌s spin flat like frisbees, and the ones that miss settle on the ground before fading.
The first 💌 invites: speech bubbles, the affection meter and the creatures' state looks, side by side.
Blows now knock the witch back and stagger her, with the biggest shoves from charging boars.
Leash physics: slack leashes curve higher and flatten out as they pull taut.
Legend buffs stacked up: with several happy legends, her 💌 volleys fan, echo and orbit all at once.
Losing a soundsystem now hurries the next wave 60 seconds closer, with a red flash on the countdown bar so you feel it.
A new guest joins the party with a burst of amber twinkles.
Party animals far from the witch travel quietly along area borders rather than cutting straight through the wild; here a traveller's straight line is compared with the border route it actually walks.
A party relic's glint seen from the treetops through a gap in the canopy: the little four-point star is how a sharp-eyed witch spots one from above.
Sigil weight made visible: the more creatures on her leash, the more the stack over her head sags, the threads pull taut and she leans into her flight.
The creature state looks on the ground: wild, happy, leashed, enraged and dazed, each readable at a glance.
From the treetops, leashed and happy creatures' sigils float above them, so she can find her party animals from on high.
The island's beach from above, first version: an even ring of sand.
The same island after: wide bays, narrows and rocky stretches where the sand almost vanishes.
An early legend dream: a sleeping legend's thought bubble shows the creature it longs for, pointing toward where to find one.
The first quest: a sleeping legend dreams of a creature, shown as a sigil in its thought bubble.
Bring that creature to it and the legend wakes happy, making its whole area friendly.
Before: home's area was just one patch of the map beside the dancefloor.
After: home became the whole circle round the dancefloor, out past the treehouse, so the party starts at the centre of everything.
The map before and after: home (green) grows into a round area centred on the dancefloor.
Walking into a legend's clearing, before: just another bit of forest.
After: stepping in brings an eerie twilight, rising motes, and the forest beyond going dark.
Ley line routes before, over many seeds: a tangle that crossed itself everywhere.
After: the whole route shown all the time, untangled so it never crosses itself.
Then varied: sweeps, lobes and combs, so each run's route has its own shape.
In game, before the untangling: ley lines criss-crossing the whole sky.
After: one calm route winding through the runestones.
Each half-buried party relic has its sigil on the ground just south of it; stand on it and pick it up like any other sigil, then carry it to a sleeping legend.
A legendary sigil put down on the ground opens as a magic circle of rune bands round the witch.
Normal, slowed, normal: the same spot outside and inside a legend's circle, the world beyond its edge drained of colour.
Walking into a sleeping legend's circle: the world outside greys and cools as time slows to a crawl, then warms again as she steps out.
The treehouse moved due north of the dancefloor, so the first ley line runs straight south from it across the clearing.
An early look at home: the witch at her decks on the treehouse balcony, wrapped in fairy lights, with the debug numbers still running down the corner.
The witch talking a creature round, emoji bubbles taking turns. Talk long enough and it joins her party and follows on her leash.
The first ley line: a glowing green-gold thread winding through the treetops toward the next area to party.
Fly out past the edge of the island and the witch lands on the sand, lies down and gazes up at the stars.
A beach witch lying alone on the sand: land by her, keep still, and she comes over to chat and stargaze.
Standing in a legend's circle, a note beside it explains what the legend wants and names the boon it will grant.
The legend circle explainer beside a sleeping fox legend, spelling out how to wake it happy and what boon it gives.
Legends made readable in their circles: a neon outline, a light floor and a soft ground glow (right) where before they were lost in the dark (left).
The ley line's pulse travelling from the dancefloor toward the next soundsystem, arriving just as the wave does.
Ley lines glowing across the forest from the treetops, linking the runestones in wave order.
The edge of the new circular map in play: the forest thins out at the rim of the world.
The map goes round: the old square forest beside the new circular island, ringed by a buffer the witch can't fly past.
A legend's dream turned to nightmare: a restless legend's angry bubble, with the creature it longs for.
The party legend, a hidden Easter egg: a hundred 💌s to win it over, a giant hat, and a leash it simply won't be pulled by.
The party's over: instead of a game-over screen, an afterparty where everyone heads home to sleep.
The lights go out in a ripple and the guests curl up asleep round the treehouse.
The party's over from the treetops: the dancefloor goes dark under the moon.
Knocked down, the witch now comes back seated behind her decks in the treehouse, just as at the start of a run.
